title: Heterogeneous Workload Shadow Orchestration and Telemetry Spec
author: Aisha Romero
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a standardized orchestration and telemetry specification for running 'shadow' evaluations across heterogeneous customer workloads (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, multi-turn stateful flows) and across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce actionable, production-realistic signal for model promotion, quantization impact, and regression triage while preserving privacy and minimizing production risk.

Scope: eval harness components, sampling strategies, fingerprinting and workload signatures, capacity-aware routing, telemetry schema, data retention, onboarding steps, and remediation/fast-fail playbook. This is intended for ML Engineers, SREs, and Product owners responsible for model promotion and quality guardrails.

High-level principles

- Non-disruptive: Shadow traffic must not add user-visible latency or affect customer SLOs.
- Representative: Sampling must preserve distributional properties of the target workload (intent mix, sequence length, token distribution).
- Traceable: Every shadow request is tagged with identifiers that tie back to deployment configuration, quant profile, and sampling provenance.
- Cost-aware: Orchestrator must throttle shadow replication under capacity pressure.
- Privacy-first: Use local PII filtering and differential-privacy sampling when required by customer configuration.

Architecture and components

1) Mirroring Proxy (mirrord)
- Deployed as an ingress-layer sidecar or region-edge service.
- Responsible for duplicating production requests to a shadow queue without affecting production response path.
- Tags traffic with: workload_fingerprint, sample_bucket_id, region, model_variant, quant_profile.

2) Shadow Sampler (sampler-service)
- Implements sampling policies (fixed-rate, stratified, capacity-aware, slot-based).
- Maintains per-workload counters and safety budgets.
- Supports on-the-fly rate adjustments via the Control Plane.

3) Replay Store (replay-blob / kafka topics)
- Short-term durable store for shadow payloads (30–90 days depending on retention policy).
- Indexes by fingerprint and sample_bucket.

4) Eval Runner (evald)
- Pulls from Replay Store, executes against target model variant(s) and quant profiles, produces evaluation artifacts.
- Runs both lightweight (latency/throughput) and fidelity evals (semantic-similarity, task-specific metrics).

5) Telemetry Collector (telemetry ingestion layer)
- Central schema-enforced collector that receives delta metrics, logs, and artifacts.
- Emits normalized events to observability pipeline and to the eval dashboard.

6) Audit & Triage UI (eval-console)
- Surface diffs between baseline and candidate variants, grouped by fingerprint slice and quant-profile.
- Provides explainability overlays and links to raw artifacts.

Workload fingerprinting (why and how)

- Fingerprinting objective: group similar requests so shadow sampling preserves within-slice distributions and we can prioritize critical slices.
- Fingerprint components: route_id, intent_hash (top-level classification of user intent), token_length_bucket, device_context (web/mobile/api), language, privacy_flag.
- Implementation: deterministic hash of normalized request headers + canonicalized prompt text (PII redacted).

Sampling strategies

1) Capacity-Aware Stratified Sampling (default)
- Stratify by fingerprint slice (intent + length bucket + language).
- Allocate sampling budget proportional to slice-contribution to production traffic, with minimum floor to ensure coverage of low-frequency critical slices.
- Backpressure: when GPU pools approach 85% utilization, reduce non-critical slice replication by multiplicative decrease.

2) Focused Safety Sampling
- For newly onboarded prompt sets or after model changes, temporarily boost sampling for slices tagged as safety-sensitive by product owners.

3) Weighted Reservoir for Long-Tail
- Maintain a small reservoir of long-tail examples sampled uniformly across customers; useful for regression discovery.

4) Differential Privacy-Constrained Sampling
- Optionally enabled per-customer: samples are drawn in a way that enforces local epsilon budgets; shadow artifacts are tagged and processed under private lanes.

Telemetry schema (key events and fields)

All telemetry events use the eval_event schema v2. Fields below are top-level strings or simple numeric values; evaluators must surface them in dashboards.

- event_type: "shadow_request" | "eval_result" | "model_diff" | "resource_pressure"
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- request_id: unique id (matches production request)
- workload_fingerprint: string
- sample_bucket_id: string
- route_id: string
- model_variant: string (e.g. redwood-phi-3b-v2)
- quant_profile: string (e.g. q4_0_dynamic)
- deployment_mode: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end execution on shadow path)
- tokens_consumed: integer
- similarity_score: float (-1..1) // semantic similarity to baseline output if applicable
- fidelity_delta: float // positive means candidate improved against baseline on chosen metric
- failure_code: string | null
- privacy_flag: true|false
- capacity_flag: OK | THROTTLED | DROPPED

(Example JSON event)
{
  "event_type": "eval_result",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-22T14:33:12Z",
  "request_id": "r-7f3c2a",
  "workload_fingerprint": "intent=translate;len=short;lang=es",
  "model_variant": "redwood-phi-3b-v2",
  "quant_profile": "q4_0_dynamic",
  "latency_ms": 42,
  "tokens_consumed": 34,
  "similarity_score": 0.92,
  "fidelity_delta": -0.03
}

Acceptance criteria and thresholds

- Latency: shadow RTT should not add > 0.5ms to production P50 or cause more than 0.1% of production requests to breach P99 latency.
- Fidelity regression: for any critical slice, fidelity_delta must be >= -0.02 averaged across a 24h window, otherwise fail promotion.
- Embeddings drift: cosine similarity mean should not drop by > 0.015 on embedding baselines for core slices.
- Reranker NDCG: candidate should not degrade NDCG@10 by more than 0.01 for top-customer slices.

Config table (example)

- job_id: string (eval-job-2025-11-02-01)
- target_variants: [baseline, candidate] (as comma-separated string)
- slices: comma-separated list of fingerprint slices
- sampling_policy: capacity_aware|focused_safety|reservoir
- retention_days: numeric (30|90)
- max_parallel_jobs: numeric
- min_samples_per_slice: numeric

Example eval job YAML (for evalctl)

eval_job: eval-job-hetero-2025-11-02
target_variants: baseline=candidate: redwood-phi-3b-v1, candidate: redwood-phi-3b-v2
slices: intent:translate:len:short, intent:qa:len:medium
sampling_policy: capacity_aware
retention_days: 30
min_samples_per_slice: 100

CLI example

# create a shadow eval job from a sample policy
evalctl create --job eval-job-hetero-2025-11-02 --policy capacity_aware --slices "translate:short,qa:medium" --variants "baseline=redwood-phi-3b-v1,candidate=redwood-phi-3b-v2"

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

1) Workload annotation (owner: product/solutions)
- Define critical slices and expected behaviors. Tag prompts that are safety or compliance sensitive.
2) Fingerprint validation (owner: ML infra)
- Run offline fingerprint sampler on representative logs to ensure slice coverage and avoid over-fragmentation.
3) Sampling policy selection (owner: ML Engineer)
- Choose capacity_aware for steady-state workloads; focused_safety for new model releases; reservoir for exploratory audits.
4) Capacity planning (owner: SRE)
- Pre-allocate GPU pools for evald with a target headroom of 30% for burst.
5) Dry-run shadow (owner: ML Engineer)
- Run a 4-hour dry-run at 1% replication, inspect telemetry and ensure no production impacts.
6) Promote to full shadow (owner: product)
- Gradually increase replication to target; monitor fidelity deltas and capacity signals.

Regression triage fast path

If a regression is detected (fidelity_delta < threshold for critical slice):
1) Auto-throttle: Control Plane marks candidate as THROTTLED for new shadow replication.
2) Bisect: Launch a binary search over recent commits/quant profiles using the automated-regression-bisect assistant (see related page).
3) Localize slice: Use the eval-console to iterate on top-10 failing fingerprints and export 500 raw artifacts for human annotation.
4) Remediate: If regression is due to quant profile, revert to previous quant_profile for the slice or pin routing to baseline model_variant; file an incident per incident playbook.

Operational runbooks (runbook excerpt)

- Incident: Shadow-agent causing production latency increase
  1. SRE alert triggers when duplicate-path latency delta > 0.5ms sustained for 5 minutes.
  2. Run: curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/shadow/adjust --data '{"action":"throttle","target":"all"}'
  3. Verify production latency returns to baseline; roll back throttling only after 15 minutes of stable metrics.

Ownership and governance

- Ownership: ML Infrastructure owns Mirror Proxy + Sampler. Eval Platform team owns Eval Runner and Telemetry pipeline. Product/Applied ML owns slice definitions and acceptance criteria. SRE owns capacity and incident response.
- Review cadence: Quarterly reviews of fingerprint schema and sampling budgets. Post-release safety window: 14 days with elevated sampling on safety slices.

Privacy and retention notes

- PII redaction: The Mirroring Proxy must run the PII redaction pipeline for any customer with privacy_flag=true before storing payloads.
- Retention: Default retention is 30 days for shadow artifacts; extended retention requires customer consent and security review.

Appendices

A. Example fingerprint canonicalization pseudo-code

1. normalize = remove_dynamic_tokens(request.text)
2. redact = run_pii_redactor(normalize)
3. fingerprint = sha256(route_id + "|" + intent_class(redact) + "|" + length_bucket(redact))

B. Prioritized metric matrix (example)

- safety: false_negative_rate | threshold: < 0.01 | action: stop promotion
- semantic_fidelity: similarity_score | threshold: >= -0.02 | action: investigate if violated
- latency: p99 | threshold: increase < 0.5ms vs baseline | action: throttle shadowing

C. Frequently asked questions

Q: Will shadowing increase costs for the customer?
A: No customer-facing billing changes; internal cost is charged to platform evaluation budget. Customers can opt out per route.

Q: What if the shadow job reveals a reproducible bug?
A: Follow the regression triage fast path and open a public incident if customer-facing.
